text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans told a press conference that he would not resign despite a finding by the prosecutor's office he had breached the anti-corruption law.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele, on holiday, has not so far familiarized himself with the conclusion given by the prosecutor's office.

- Krishtopans' party, Latvia's Way, stressed that the minister should not resign as he has committed only formal infringements of the law. The party warned Shkele the government would be threatened if he forced Krishtopans to quit.
- German authorities have confirmed they arrested Armands Stendzenieks, a debtor of the collapsed Banka Baltija. He may be extradited in a month.
- The newspaper said in an editorial that Krishtopans should go, saying all other ministers who broke the anti-corruption law had quit.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said it was too early to say for sure that Latvia would not be invited to start talks with the EU in the first phase of enlargement and that the final decision will only be taken at the end of the year.

- The liquidator of Banka Baltija, David Berry told Diena that it was the former administrator of the bank, Uldis Grube, and lawyer Andris Grutups, who helped him to take the decision to write-off $10 million owed to the bank by electricity supplier Latvenergo.
- Latvia and Sweden signed an agreement to open in Riga another higher education institute, the Higher School of Law.

- According to unofficial sources, the Estonian police have arrested the scandalous Internet blackmailer Viktor, who had repeatedly threatened to blow up stores and a supermarket, as well as hotels in Riga.
